correctness.rationale: The two-time innovation relation Y_t=q Y_0+eta_t, q=exp(-gamma t), eta_t independent of Y_0 and centered with variance Var(Y_0)(1-q^2), gives E[Y0 Yt^3]-E[Y0^3 Yt]=-(q-q^3)(E[Y0^4]-3 Var(Y0)^2). The Poisson stochastic-convolution fourth cumulant is lambda E[J^4]/(4 gamma) and thermal Brownian noise contributes none. Maximizing q-q^3 yields q=1/sqrt(3), proving both peak and inverse formulas. Stationary time reversal makes the fourth joint-cumulant swap of independent added V vanish, while pair-partition terms cancel because the covariance is stationary; independent mixed cumulants add and K_{p,q}=q^q kappa_{p+q}. These are exact identities for symmetric/asymmetric marks, including nonzero mean after centering. Independently used exact symbolic cumulant and innovation calculations and checked the maximum, invertibility and noise cancellation for representative parameters. Unlike a simulation this reconstructs the general proof.

final_claim: For the stationary centered Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process with Brownian thermal noise and independent Poisson kicks with finite fourth mark moment, the fourth chronological asymmetry is Delta(t)=-(lambda E[J^4]/(4 gamma)) exp(-gamma t)(1-exp(-2 gamma t)); its unique maximal magnitude is at log(3)/(2 gamma), and its exact population signal is invariant under independent stationary reversible observation noise. The mixed-cumulant hierarchy follows under corresponding moment hypotheses.
limitations: Strict sign requires nonzero kick marks with positive probability; the stationary state and finite fourth mark moment are essential.
Ideal population-correlation maximum need not optimize finite-sample estimation variance, and gamma and aggregate kick intensity only are identifiable.
